description: One deployable split into modules with explicit public APIs and owned data. The recommended default for most teams.
Independently deployable services that own their data and talk over the network. Solve team scaling at the cost of distributed-systems complexity.
Code runs per request or event on a managed platform that scales to zero; trade-offs are cold starts, limits and vendor coupling.
Ports and adapters: the domain defines interfaces, infrastructure implements them, dependencies point inward.
Data in different parts of the system converges after a delay instead of being updated in one transaction.
Save outgoing events in the same database transaction as the change, then publish them, so data and events never diverge.
Systems mirror the communication structure of the organization that builds them.
